clue.text: Set of items put behind somewhere filthy for hairdresser

indicators.note: placing one thing behind another sets the order of the two parts, the second following the first

parts.note: a pigsty is a byword for a filthy place
a list is a set of items written down

explanation.surface: Someone sets out a hairdresser's kit in a grubby back room.
explanation.walkthrough: The set of items comes first in the clue but goes second in the answer, because it is put behind the filthy place.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylist is someone who cuts and styles hair for a living, the usual salon job title.

clue.text: Casual worker starts to unpick really appetising Japanese dish

parts.note: a temp is a temporary or casual employee

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A casual kitchen worker starts to pick at a delicious Japanese dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unpick' looks like a verb the worker performs, but it only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is a Japanese preparation of seafood or vegetables fried in light batter.

clue.text: Delicate thing that might be struck?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a flame struck from a match

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests something fragile that could be hit; the second meaning comes from the phrase 'strike a light', meaning ignite a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means gentle or not heavy as an adjective, and as a noun a flame or match one can strike.

clue.text: Orangey flavouring for fans varied

indicators.note: something varied has been changed about, so these letters come in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An orange-coloured flavouring is offered to fans in several varieties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For fans' reads like the audience for the flavouring, but the two words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a costly spice from crocus stigmas that colours and flavours rice an orange-yellow.

clue.text: Bachelor keeps getting excited about round made for a particular customer

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another
excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A single man keeps getting worked up about a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of 'keeps' wrap around the round letter, all after the bachelor's B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke tailoring is cut to one client's order rather than bought off the peg.

clue.text: Eastern writer with regret regularly gets to appear

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
the writer of a clue refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: An oriental author, full of remorse, steadily comes out into the open.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'writer' or 'setter' often means the setter, giving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come into view or come out, the same as to appear.

clue.text: A spree Viv arranged to become widespread

indicators.note: arranging things puts them into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Viv organised a shopping spree that caught on everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd name Viv is there only to supply letters, a sure sign of anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pervasive spreads through every part, so it is found widely throughout.

clue.text: Most enthusiastic king has three points established

parts.note: K is king in chess notation
three compass points: east, east, north
est. is the abbreviation for established

explanation.surface: An eager monarch has set out three founding principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' in crosswords are usually compass points; any three that fit will do, here east twice and then north.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen means eager or enthusiastic, and the superlative form means the most eager of all.

clue.text: Minor actor with alternative record around November that's remarkable

indicators.note: to go around something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: an extra is a non-speaking film or stage performer
or introduces an alternative
a diary is a daily record
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A bit-part actor with another recording from November turns out to be impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: The record goes around the November letter, placed after the actor and the alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraordinary means beyond the ordinary, so worthy of comment or notice, which is what remarkable means.

clue.text: Self-satisfied sergeant major outwardly unappealing

parts.note: SM is the abbreviation for sergeant major

indicators.note: the outward part of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A complacent sergeant major who looks thoroughly unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly unappealing' reads as a description of his looks, but it asks for just the outer letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes someone excessively pleased with themselves, a close synonym of complacent.

clue.text: Make a mistake blocking novel exit for dog

indicators.note: blocking a path means standing in the middle of it, so one piece sits inside another
novel means new, so these letters take on a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Getting something wrong stands in the way of a fresh way out for a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word joining the clue to its definition, but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox terrier is a small breed of terrier, originally used to drive foxes from their earths.

clue.text: Fool here essentially gets to speak in a barely audible voice

definitions.text: speak in a barely audible voice

parts.note: mutt is slang for a stupid person

indicators.note: the essence of a thing is its core, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters

explanation.surface: An idiot standing here has to speak very quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: Mutt usually means a mongrel dog, but it is also slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutter is to talk in a low, indistinct way, often grumbling under one's breath.

clue.text: Engineer agreed to enter road given a new assessment?

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road

indicators.note: to engineer something is to contrive or rework it, so these letters are reconstructed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A civil engineer consents to go onto a road that has been re-surveyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' wants to be the noun RE, the Royal Engineers; here it is a verb telling you to rework 'agreed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something regraded has been placed in a fresh grade or category after evaluation, like a reclassified road or exam.

clue.text: Tom in band played a racket sport

indicators.note: something played has been performed or toyed with, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tom, a member of a pop group, took up a racket sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' seems to be about the band making music; it signals the reordering of the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a game played with rackets and a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Drawing power in team's MG in a fancy guise

indicators.note: a fancy guise is a costume or disguise, so the letters appear dressed up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A team's MG sports car in fancy livery has real pulling power with the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: MG is a British sports-car make, here used only for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetism is the force by which magnets attract, and figuratively personal charm that draws people.

clue.text: Same thing again defended by pundit today

indicators.note: defenders surround what they protect, so the letters sit enclosed within the words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A television pundit today backs up the same point once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the gap between the two final words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to indicate that something already said applies again, a repetition.

clue.text: Inferior guide's coat has sign of identification

parts.note: bad means of poor quality

indicators.note: a coat is an outer layer, so only the outside letters are taken

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A second-rate tour guide's jacket carries an ID tag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coat' looks like a garment, but it means the outer layer of the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is a pin or emblem worn to show who you are or which group you belong to.

clue.text: Friend wearing gold ring initially like a non-professional?

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a mate is a friend

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only a first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pal wearing a gold ring at first glance looks like a hobbyist.
explanation.walkthrough: The friend sits inside the gold symbol, and the first letter of ring follows.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, amateur describes something done unpaid or unskilfully, the way a hobbyist rather than an expert would do it.

clue.text: Journalist left among sheep is beginning to survey mountain plant

parts.note: an ed. or editor is a journalist

indicators.note: to be among things is to be surrounded by them, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A reporter abandoned among a flock is starting to study an alpine flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The left letter goes inside the sheep, and the result follows the journalist; 'left' reads as abandoned but is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is a white woolly-leaved flower native to the high Alps.

clue.text: Line, say, followed by friendly country in a permissible fashion

parts.note: a leg is one stretch of a route, as a line is on a map; 'say' marks the example
an ally is a nation on friendly terms

explanation.surface: A border line is drawn, then a friendly nation signs off on it lawfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is loose: a leg of a journey is one line of travel, and 'say' warns the link is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally means within the law, so done in a way that is allowed or permitted.

clue.text: Lean son overlooking bank, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down entry, a thing overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a bank is one example of a moneylender, as 'perhaps' signals

explanation.surface: A thin son looks out over a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a river, but it is the financial kind, which lends money.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slim and thin, a close synonym of lean as an adjective.

clue.text: Bishop introducing different trouble

indicators.note: to introduce something is to bring it in after you, so the first piece leads the second

parts.note: B is bishop in chess notation
other means different

explanation.surface: A bishop brings in some new kind of difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different' wants to be an anagram signal; here it simply means other.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother is effort, fuss or annoyance, the same sense as trouble in 'it's no trouble'.

clue.text: Anxious racer now after a crash

indicators.note: a crash leaves things smashed and scattered, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A racing driver is nervous after an accident on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is slightly loose: careworn is worn out by worry rather than simply anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Careworn describes someone showing the strain of prolonged worry, a weary form of being troubled.

clue.text: Some began nettling seabird

indicators.note: only some of the words is needed, a stretch of consecutive letters

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone started irritating a seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The gannet is a large white diving bird of northern coasts and seas.

clue.text: Loop shortly arising close to home

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: soon means shortly, before long

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A circular route that will soon come up near your house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to home' reads as nearby, but means the final letter of home.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot that tightens when pulled.

clue.text: Minor keyboard, maybe

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a device attached to a computer, of which a keyboard is one example

explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor keyboard' sounds like music, a piano piece in a minor key; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means marginal or secondary; as a noun it is any add-on computer device such as a mouse or printer.

clue.text: Chances characterising one leader of students

parts.note: one is an odd number, so odd is what characterises it

indicators.note: the leader of a group is at the front, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: The prospects of becoming a head student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characterising one' is a cryptic hint: the quality that describes the number one is that it is odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the likelihood or probability of something happening, as in betting.

clue.text: Foremost pair, one linked to Joseph's partner

parts.note: pr is the abbreviation for pair
I is the Roman numeral one
Mary was the wife of Joseph in the Nativity story

explanation.surface: The leading couple, one of them married to Joseph, as in a nativity play.
explanation.walkthrough: PR is a standard abbreviation for pair, as on shoe boxes and price tags.
explanation.definitionFit: Primary means first in importance or rank, the chief or principal one.

clue.text: British yard found beside centre from memory

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
y is the abbreviation for yard
the heart of something is its centre

explanation.surface: A British courtyard is located next to the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests a garden or courtyard, but it is the unit of length abbreviated to Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something by heart is to have learned it so well you can recite it unprompted.
